title: Planting Calendar for Timor-Leste
summary: The wet season (November–April) drives the main planting; dry-season crops depend on irrigation.
actions: Maize, beans, cassava and sweet potato: plant at the start of the rains, November–December (later in the south coast)
Rice: nursery in November–December, transplant December–January; a second crop is possible in irrigated areas around May
Tomato and chili: best in the dry season (May–September) with irrigation, or under rain shelter
Leafy vegetables: year round near water
Watch the first rains: plant after 2–3 good rains have soaked the soil, not after the first shower

sections.heading: Wet season (Nov–Apr)
sections.body: Maize, beans, cassava, sweet potato and rice. Plant after the soil is properly wet.

sections.heading: Dry season (May–Oct)
sections.body: Tomato, chili and vegetables on irrigated plots. Second rice crop where irrigation allows.

title: Choosing and Saving Seed
summary: Good seed is the cheapest yield increase: select from the best plants, dry well and store sealed.
actions: Mark the healthiest, most productive plants in the field before harvest and keep their seed
Dry seed in the shade until hard, then store in a sealed container with a little ash or dry sand
Test germination: plant 20 seeds in moist sand; if fewer than 16 sprout, use more seed per hole or get new seed
Buy improved seed (e.g. Sele maize, Nakroma rice) from trusted sources every few seasons

sections.heading: Selecting
sections.body: Choose seed from the best plants in the field, not from the pile after harvest.

sections.heading: Storing and testing
sections.body: Dry fully, store sealed, and test germination before planting.

title: Spacing and Depth
summary: Correct spacing gives each plant light, air and nutrients; too dense means disease and small yields.
actions: Maize: rows 75 cm, plants 25 cm, 1 plant per hole, 3–5 cm deep
Beans: rows 50 cm, plants 30 cm, 2 seeds per hole
Rice: 20 × 20 cm, 2–3 seedlings per hill, shallow
Chili: 40–50 cm each way on raised beds
Plant seed at a depth about 2–3 times its size

sections.heading: Rule of thumb
sections.body: Plant seeds 2–3 times their size deep. Space so leaves of neighbouring plants just touch at maturity.

title: Intercropping Maize and Beans
summary: Growing beans between maize rows gives two harvests, adds nitrogen and confuses pests.
actions: Plant maize first; plant beans between rows 1–2 weeks later so the maize is not shaded
Use climbing beans on the maize stalks or bush beans between rows
Harvest beans first, leaving the roots in the soil
Add pumpkin or sweet potato as a ground cover for a three-crop system

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: More food from the same land, less risk if one crop fails, and free nitrogen from the beans.

sections.heading: How
sections.body: Plant beans 1–2 weeks after maize, between the rows. Leave bean roots in the soil after harvest.
